name: Cate Le Bon
label: Mexican Summer
lede: Cate Le Bon grew up on a Welsh farm, sang on a Gruff Rhys tour, built herself a chair, and now gets the call from Wilco, Deerhunter and St. Vincent when they want to sound less like themselves.

eras.title: Backing vocals, then a patron
eras.text: Born Cate Timothy in Carmarthenshire, she borrowed her stage name from Simon Le Bon and got her first break singing behind other people. By 2009 she had a debut album and a mentor in Super Furry Animals' Gruff Rhys.

years.h: Her first record credit is backing vocals for Richard James
years.p: She sings on [[Richard James|6966324a-c29f-4b6f-92a4-5e34ad2abab3]]'s The Seven Sleepers Den, credited under her birth name, Cate Timothy. James is the singer of Gorky's Zygotic Mynci.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · NPR Music · Irish Times
years.h: Gruff Rhys takes her on tour, then takes her under his wing
years.p: She opens for [[Gruff Rhys|254caf14-7b63-47d1-aa9f-acc7cb541814]] of [[Super Furry Animals|c5f5dc27-3059-49c0-ae45-5009a01bb9ec]] on his solo UK tour. NPR reported he first spotted her at Welsh club nights.
years.xp:
Rhys described her first single, the double A-side 'No One Can Drag Me Down' and 'Disappear', as "Bobbie Gentry and Nico fight over a Casio keyboard; melody wins!" (Wikipedia).

He later lent her a house, too: the Victorian terrace in Cardiff where she wrote Pompeii belongs to Rhys, the Irish Times reported.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Her first record under her own name is sung in Welsh
years.p: The EP Edrych yn Llygad Ceffyl Benthyg comes out on Peski Records, with [[Gorky's Zygotic Mynci|4015f3f8-2711-41de-b80b-4fee07373b12]] players Megan Childs on violin and John Thomas on pedal steel.

years.cap: Le Bon on stage with Neon Neon, 2008
years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Irish Times
years.h: She sings 'I Lust U' on Neon Neon's Stainless Style
years.p: She is the guest voice on the single from [[Neon Neon|6191360a-edc5-41d7-a83e-c9f0ab842f53]], Gruff Rhys and Boom Bip's concept album about the DeLorean factory in Belfast.

years.src: Wikipedia: Me Oh My · NPR Music · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Me Oh My, the debut, on Irony Bored
years.p: Released 12 October 2009. Slow and dry enough that reviewers reached for Nico.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album was first going to be called Pet Deaths. A Welsh-language song, 'O am Gariad', was written for it and cut because it interrupted the flow.

NPR credited Rhys with producing it and called the result bare-bones.

eras.title: Eigg, then Los Angeles
eras.text: The second album gets busier and stranger, and in January 2013 she leaves Cardiff for California. The move brings the band, the sound and the collaborators she works with for the next decade.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cyrk · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Cyrk comes out of a stay on the Isle of Eigg
years.p: Faster and more dissonant than Me Oh My. She called it a time-travel travelogue, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she drew on the sea, wildlife and matters of the heart on Eigg in the Inner Hebrides, and rehearsed with a tight Welsh band in the mountains.

Bandcamp Daily points to the closing pair 'Ploughing Out, Pt. 1' and 'Pt. 2' as the turn: the second is fuzzy, Stereolab-ish rock with skronky saxophone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Wikipedia: Mug Museum
years.h: She leaves Wales for Los Angeles
years.p: Le Bon relocates to push her career in the US, and Mug Museum gets recorded there that spring at Seahorse Sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mug Museum · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Mug Museum is her first record on Wichita and Turnstile
years.p: Released 12 November 2013, produced by [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]] and [[Josiah Steinbrick|3143853f-44ce-49d5-b7ec-b59e8a6cf871]]. Pitchfork gave it 7.3.
years.xp: Jeremy Larson wrote in Pitchfork that it has small, graceful songs with deceptive amounts of depth. [[Stephen Black|d3789f6f-cc8d-4404-a104-103f9daa6bd3]] played bass and [[H. Hawkline|ae41819a-51e2-4f21-aa3c-b37f22b733ae]] (Huw Evans) played guitar.

years.src: NPR Music
years.h: She throws about 150 ceramic mugs for the pre-orders
years.p: NPR reported she made the mugs herself for the Mug Museum campaign. The title came from a former roommate's name for the pile of teacups in her bedroom.

eras.title: A furniture course interrupts the band
eras.text: She finds the people she will keep working with, Tim Presley among them, then steps away from touring to study woodworking. The chair she builds becomes the picture of her next record.

years.src: NPR Music · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]]'s band opens for her in LA, and they become DRINKS
years.p: Presley and Le Bon record Hermits on Holiday as DRINKS, released on Heavenly Recordings in August 2015. NPR premiered the title track in May.
years.xp:
Presley told NPR she completely rearranged one of his songs and made it ten million times better than what he had. Le Bon said the project reignited her love of writing and performing.

Bandcamp Daily called it lean and loose, two fringe-pop wizards in experimental mode. NPR premiered the title track in May 2015. Presley, of [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]] and [[Darker My Love|15c5c0de-b8ff-49ab-8a58-506c89453f03]], would later be her partner for years.

years.cap: Le Bon at the Cluny, Newcastle, on the Crab Day tour, 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Crab Day · NPR Music
years.h: Crab Day is her first record for Drag City
years.p: Released 15 April 2016, recorded at Panoramic House in Stinson Beach, California, with [[Stella Mozgawa|f578d602-2ed4-4ec4-a0a7-1947cb01ac44]] on drums and Black on bass. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Laura Snapes wrote in Pitchfork that it is a voyage into doubt led by a queasy compass.

NPR reported she called it the first record she has made with no inhibition at all, and that it felt like a band's record rather than hers.

years.cap: Le Bon live in Cardigan, Wales, 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · NPR Music
years.h: The Crab Day band tours as BANANA, in mohair hats
years.p: A five-piece that improvises: Le Bon, Black, Evans, [[Josh Klinghoffer|3f6e1477-03dc-4117-ac15-ec53b776e9a0]] and Steinbrick. A BANANA live album follows on Leaving Records in 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Rock Pool arrives on Drag City in January
years.p: Four tracks, including her version of 'I Just Want to Be Good', written for Sweet Baboo's 2015 album The Boombox Ballads.

years.big: "disgruntled accountants, retired dentists, a real pick-and-mix of people"
years.src: Rolling Stone · Irish Times
years.h: She quits the road for a year of furniture school
years.p: Le Bon on her classmates, to Rolling Stone. Burnt out, she spends a year on a woodworking course in the Lake District, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and writes Reward on a secondhand piano between classes.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reported the course ran to a strict schedule and was "incredible and at times quite challenging", in her words. When it finished she built a chair in dark-stained oak.

She told the magazine the chair looked like the record sounded in her mind. It lives at her parents' house in West Wales.

eras.title: A new label, a desert, a Mercury nomination
eras.text: A new label, a duo record, a desert session with Bradford Cox, and the piano album that gets her nominated for the Mercury Prize. She also starts producing other people's records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hippo Lite
years.h: DRINKS follow up with Hippo Lite, and Pitchfork gives it 8.0
years.p: Released 20 April 2018 on Drag City. Reviews ran from 3/10 at Exclaim! to 9/10 at Loud and Quiet.
years.xp: Black engineered it, per Wikipedia, and John Thomas II played extra drums. A DIY reviewer praised "moments of sheer chaotic genius married with brilliant songwriting".

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She moves from Drag City to Mexican Summer
years.p: The Brooklyn label goes on to release Reward, Pompeii and Michelangelo Dying.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Wikipedia: Michelangelo Dying
years.h: She plays the Barbican with John Cale and an orchestra
years.p: [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] and the London Contemporary Orchestra share the stage with her. Cale comes back in 2025 to sing on Michelangelo Dying.

years.src: Stereogum · Bandcamp Daily · Rolling Stone
years.h: Bradford Cox picks her for Deerhunter at Marfa Myths
years.p: [[Bradford Cox|da7eb8d4-4a74-474f-b907-c38d2355b72b]] told Stereogum she would produce the next [[Deerhunter|4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b]] record in Marfa, Texas, informed by the desert around it. The pair also record a quick-and-loose EP, Myths 004.
years.xp:
Cox said there is a feeling of disappearance in Marfa, and that the desert has a lot of disappeared things in it. That became the title of the album.

Le Bon called Myths 004 a "crude holiday scrapbook" of studio jams, per Bandcamp Daily.

years.cap: Le Bon and band at Portland House, Cardiff, on the last night of the 2019 UK tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.h: She co-produces Deerhunter's Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.p: Released 18 January 2019 on 4AD, with sessions in Marfa and Atlanta. Le Bon also plays harpsichord and mandolin, and sings on it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits her as co-producer with Ben H. Allen III, Ben Etter and the band. She plays harpsichord on 'Death in Midsummer', sings on 'Tarnung' and plays mandolin on 'No One's Sleeping'.

Pitchfork gave the album 8.0.

years.cap: Le Bon and her band on the Reward tour, 3 November 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Reward · Rolling Stone · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Reward is the piano record that gets her a Mercury Prize nomination
years.p: Released 24 May 2019 on Mexican Summer. Pitchfork gave it 8.4.
years.xp:
Produced by Le Bon, [[Samur Khouja|a6f84fad-37f1-4d77-8ab1-38c93cdc81fc]] and Josiah Steinbrick. [[Kurt Vile|e07a111e-4e8a-4651-a849-01ac60551ab2]] sings on one track; Klinghoffer, Mozgawa, Black and Hawkline play.

Sessions ran at Stinson Beach in May, in LA, and in Joshua Tree that August. Of the LA sessions she told Rolling Stone: "Everything went to shit."

eras.title: Stranded in Cardiff
eras.text: A producer's gig in Iceland ends with Le Bon locked down in Wales. The album she writes there makes Pitchfork's best of 2022.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Irish Times
years.h: Lockdown catches her in Iceland, producing John Grant
years.p: She is working on [[John Grant|27ca9c68-650a-4659-b8ef-013e5698ff55]]'s Boy from Michigan when the borders close behind her, the Irish Times reported.

years.cap: Le Bon live in Hackney, 15 March 2022
q: Cate Le Bon on Pompeii ruins (Irish Times)
years.src: Wikipedia: Pompeii · Album of the Year · BrooklynVegan: Pitchfork's · Irish Times
years.h: Pompeii gets written in an old Cardiff terrace
years.p: Released 4 February 2022 on Mexican Summer. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and ranked it No. 20 of 2022.
years.xp:
Jenn Pelly called it a "wondrous sixth album" in the Pitchfork review. Metacritic scores it 85. It also placed 10th at Treble, 15th at Paste and 21st at Mojo.

Le Bon wrote it in the Victorian terrace in Cardiff she lived in 15 years earlier, with Tim Presley and producer Khouja. Recording took in studios in Wales, Sydney and London; Mozgawa plays drums, and Euan Hinshelwood and Black play saxophone.

years.src: Exclaim!
years.h: 'Moderation' becomes the second Pompeii single
years.p: Exclaim! ran the video, calling it the second offering from her upcoming sixth album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She produces Vile's 'Jesus on a Wire'
years.p: Wikipedia lists the song on [[Kurt Vile|e07a111e-4e8a-4651-a849-01ac60551ab2]]'s Watch My Moves among her production credits. Vile had sung on her Reward.

eras.title: Everybody's producer
eras.text: She becomes the first outside producer Wilco has used since 2007, works with Devendra Banhart and Horsegirl, and releases the album she made after her breakup with Tim Presley.

years.src: BrooklynVegan: Wilco · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Wilco bring in an outside producer for the first time since 2007: her
years.p: Cousin is out 29 September 2023 on dBpm. Le Bon brings synths, drum machines and saxophonist Euan Hinshelwood into the band.
years.xp:
BrooklynVegan reported it was Wilco's first album with an outside producer since Sky Blue Sky. [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]] is quoted by Bandcamp Daily: "I would love to work with Cate on anything."

Tweedy has also praised her guitar playing: "Whenever I try to figure out her parts, they're way harder than they sound." (Wikipedia)

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She produces Devendra Banhart, A. Savage and Vile again
years.p: Banhart's Flying Wig, [[A. Savage|5bee43cb-a3a0-47bb-9cc6-662a90ce4380]]'s Several Songs About Fire and Vile's Back to Moon Beach all carry her name.
years.xp: [[Devendra Banhart|0110e63e-0a9b-4818-af8e-41e180c20b9a]] told Bandcamp Daily she is the only person he wanted to make the record with.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She plays bass on St. Vincent's All Born Screaming
years.p: Bass on two songs, and an additional production credit on four of [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]]'s, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Le Bon and her live band at Llais, Cardiff, 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Michelangelo Dying · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: After the breakup, Michelangelo Dying
years.p: Released 26 September 2025, with John Cale singing on 'Ride'. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Wikipedia quotes Le Bon describing it as realising you have abandoned yourself in all-encompassing love, and the breakup as an amputation you don't want but know will save you.

It was planned for 2024 and delayed by illness and exhaustion after the relationship ended. Sessions took in Cardiff, Hydra, London and Los Angeles, with Samur Khouja producing.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Horsegirl let her in as a fourth collaborator
years.p: Drummer Gigi Reece said Le Bon is the first person the Chicago band allowed that role, on Phonetics On and On, which she produced.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She produces Dry Cleaning's third album, Secret Love
years.p: Leftover sessions yield 'Always the Same', a single with St. Vincent.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
